utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we -- Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness Mr. Clark be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we start if we could just take care of one matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the spirit if expediting issues, if I could just reference exactly what we're talking about so I can discuss it with the chamber, and if we could bring P1256 on the screen, page 10 of that document. These are the photographs that the Prosecutor went through yesterday, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Examples of the various type of findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I sent an e-mail to the Prosecutor. This is KN01/317, and according to the clarification schedule, KN01/317 is Stoja, S-t-o-j-a, Jaric, J-a-r-i-c. And according to the clarification schedule and again, Judge, this is the additional victims that -- of course that we haven't exhaustively gone through this. Individual was killed in Donja Tiskovac. Donja Tiskovac is in Bosnia-Herzegovina and which is not part of this particular indictment. Likewise, it is dated 5 August 1995, and I know the Prosecutor will agree that the HV was not in Donja Tiskovac and 5 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, first of all, is there agreement on the place where this person had died?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. There's agreement on the place where the person died, and there's agreement in respect of the presence of the HV on the 7th of August and not before the 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that this 317 B could not be considered to be a victim in the context of the indictment or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: We -- the specific question that we've answered this morning is our agreement discussed with the Defence this morning is our position in regard to the presence of the HV and our position in regard to the date of death. And what we've indicated is we can agree the position in regard to the HV, and we cannot agree that the 5th of August reflects the precise date of death. Insofar as the issue of the geographic location and the -- whether or not that is covered by the indictment. I need to consult with my colleagues answering that question. I haven't addressed that issue this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I understood the series of photographs, and I'm honest in saying this. Yesterday it came into my mind that it is almost part of what could have been a book on forensic examination of bodily remains, rather than being specific on 713 because it was not presented to us because 317 would need some specific attention in evidentiary -- in an evidentiary context, but rather to give examples which could have been taken from any other book and is not directly related to the victims in this case, to the extent that there are any victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We had intended just because of the limited time, of course, the evidence in relation to the specific killings has come in pursuant to the 25 November decision, including autopsy reports, identification forms, photographs. However, in terms of the time we wanted to take in court that was our specific purpose, merely to illustrate the nature of the materials that this particular expert had at his disposal in assembling his findings and conducting the forensic examinations in the mortuary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, with all due respect to my learned friend that may have been a tertiary reason. But the primary reason for this photo array was the shock value for the Chamber by putting all bodies these bodies in here in this fashion for the Chamber leading the Chamber to conclude, oh my heavens, something terrible must have happened, and the gentleman that is seated to my rear must have been responsible in some fashion. If I may, Judge, this is it an execution. Now they have had any number of years to -- to take a look at this and make a determination as to when this occurred and where it occurred. Now they agree it took place in Donja Tiskovac. But as far as the date range, there is no waffling in the document that was filed by the Office of the Prosecutor when this took place. In other instances in the clarification schedule, there are ranges of dates in and around the particular time between various states. There is a specific date here of the 5th of August, and the HV wasn't there. And the rhetorical question for my learned friend is how is the Defence supposed to answer this type of allegation which looks like an execution of this women, unquestionably at this point Serb on Serb. How were we supposed to answer that if we can't take the facts as set forth by the Prosecution. That is it what the Defence have to meet which we are attempting to meet. And we look at those facts. It is unquestionable that the HV was not in Donja Tiskovac. Putting aside the fact that Donja Tiskovac is not even in part of this indictment because it is in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your point is perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I was honest when I said yesterday that it came into my mind that book could have been taken totally unrelated because that is how I understood the testimony. At the same time, Mr. Margetts, or course it might have been better then to take a book rather than take an example of a person of which it could have been known that that person died elsewhere, and nevertheless introduce it with the KN01 numbers on it if it was just to demonstrate what kind of findings one can make.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and I would also say that we all of these photos uploaded into e-court, I believe, now, and at some stage will be reviewed by the parties and viewed by the Court. So I -- I obviously don't accept that the shock value of these photos --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not spend too much time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The second thing is, Your Honour, I would say this, that we also introduced it because these are the remains that were in this cemetery, and it did have more value in our view than merely being a forensic book from a totally disassociated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If someone was found in this cemetery which died five years before or after at a different place, then of course it's not appropriate to bring it in, Mr. Margetts because it then is exactly creates a suggestion as is heavily criticised and rightly to some extent by Mr. Kehoe. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, it is heavily criticised by Mr. Kehoe. We heard that this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. Any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further response?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No further response on this issue, Mr. President. However there is another issue that I would like to bring to the attention of the Court before the witness is called. That is, yesterday my learned friend tendered some documents relating to the circumstances of death and in -- specifically D1225 and D1229, and I had indicated to the Court that to my knowledge, having just received those documents, I didn't recognise them as materials that had previously been introduced, and were admitted pursuant to the decision of the Trial Chamber of 25 November. Having had the benefit of reviewing these materials overnight, I have now recognised that the documents introduced as D1225 and D1229 were, in fact, part of the Prosecution's motion to admit documents and were listed in Appendix D, and accordingly, those documents, whilst probably -- I haven't had the chance to consider whether they're identical. I imagine they are completely identical. The Defence's version will therefore be duplicated if they're assigned numbers when we do present the tables of materials admitted. So at the time that we present the tables of the material admitted, we may ask -- submit that. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... if they are the same, there is no need to do that. And if they are not the same, of course, there may be a reason to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if they are the same, you should leave them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they are not the same, then you should explain what the difference is and then keep them on your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any further matter we have to address before we ask Mr. Clark to enter the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: There is one further matter and that has been the subject of discussion between the parties. Yesterday there was a reference in the cross-examination to a particular body, that being the body of a Dmitar Vojnovic, and this individual was identified in the context of an autopsy report which was body KN01/162 and, secondly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it assigned a number yesterday? Would that have been D12 -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: D1227 is the circumstances of death or the death report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Identification form relating to that individual. Now that form reveals that this individual was born in 1951. Now -- and this individual that was born in 1951 is the subject of an autopsy report that's listed in the Appendix A to Dr. Clark' report, and that is the autopsy report for KN01, number 162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's D1226. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In the further particulars and the clarification of the indictment, an individual by the same name, Dmitar Vojnovic is referenced; however, the date of birth is in the year 1965. Now, there is another autopsy report that relates to that individual, that is, the Vojnovic, who was born in 1965. That is not referenced in Dr. Clark's report, and we would like the opportunity to put that autopsy report to Dr. Clark so that this matter, in relation to Mr. Vojnovic that's been raised by the Defence in the cross-examination, can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If -- if I may, Judge, on a couple of issues. The D1226 on autopsy -- excuse me, KN03/162 is listed in the annex A for Dr. Clark's report on page 20. You can see it as 162 is Dmitar Vojnovic. This is an individual who passed away on the 31st of July. If one goes back to the clarification schedule that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- let me just try to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Just if we can go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Because the date of death usually does not appear in the autopsy report, so therefore you are linking a date to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm linking it with -- Mr. President, I'm linking it with D1227, which the first page of D1227 links it to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: KN03/162. And then we go down to the next page of that, and it notes -- it -- 31st of July, 1995, Oklaj Knin, and that is the same individual who is listed in -- Dr. Clark's Annex A for KN03, and it's the last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you say on the basis of the number assigned and on the basis of the name, D1226 must deal with the same bodily remains as the bodily remains of the person described in D1227.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas Mr. Margetts now draws our attention to different years of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. If we can stay with that allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: First off, the -- if the Prosecution is arguing that the Dmitar Vojnovic that is the subject of this other autopsy is not the Dmitar Vojnovic that is in the annex, they have not included that other autopsy in their list of autopsies to be presented into evidence. Now, I can only work with what I have, and going to the clarification schedule, which, Mr. President, was filed, I take it, in July. Is that correct? It was in July. There is it a Dmitar Vojnovic on page 6 of the additional names. He is number 220. This individual is found in a Knin hospital, but there is no KN number identifying that person. So with all due respect, Mr. President, we can only work with what we have. We found a Dmitar Vojnovic who was found in the Knin hospital, 7 August, and without any other information concerning the actual autopsy and not seeing this other autopsy that Mr. Margetts is talking about because it hasn't been presented into evidence, a fortiori, we had to conclude that this was the Dmitar Vojnovic because Dr. Clark examined him and listed it in the annex in November of 2008, some four months after that clarification schedule. This other Vojnovic autopsy is KN01/399 according to my courtroom deputy, and that is not on the list. So that is the basis of how when we were trying to put these cases together and present this to the Chamber, that we came up with the idea or the conclusion that this was an individual who died on the 31st of July, 1995. Clearly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has this been discussed among the parties, the issue just raised, Mr. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It's only been raised in the last few hours by e-mail, so we haven't had a full discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about trying to see to what common conclusions, if any, you could come in the next break, because I do see that there are -- there is a -- on both sides there are reasons to believe that it is or is not the same person. Now let's see where this leads you if you have exchanged your views on the matter in more detail. Because what we're talking about now is one of the examples of where you, Mr. Kehoe, you say the additional information shows that the limited conclusions by Dr. Clark might have been different if that information would have been available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we have a few examples of that. That's important for the case. It's not the whole of the case. It is not the core of the case. Let's see to what extent you can reach common conclusions on these matter, if not, then of course the Chamber will further consider it. But then it might be a good idea to present to the Chamber where exactly the differences of views are. Yes? Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could Dr. Clark be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Clark. Please be seated. First of all, our apologies that we let you wait for almost half an hour. We had to deal with a few procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm well used to that, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not here but elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. Elsewhere, yes. Mr. Clark, I would like to remind that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Kehoe will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examination by Mr. Kehoe: [Continued}

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, if we can bring up a photograph you talked yesterday, P1256 page 10, it's the photo we just had on the screen, KN01/317. I said previously. We had it before you came out. Apologies. You recall this. You had this as a shot-gun injury, probably a handgun with a low velocity to the forehead with an exit wound in the rear.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to be precise, it's a gunshot, not shotgun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Gunshot.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a Gunshot injury, and the fact that it's -- there's so little damage with it suggested to us that this was an a handgun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. If we can turn to the autopsy report, 65 ter 6307. Doctor, this is your autopsy report signed by you for this particular woman where you reflect exactly -- it reflects exactly what we just said, a single injury to the head almost certainly a handgun. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer 65 ter 6307 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is already in evidence but has not been assigned a number yet. If I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll just check Appendix A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or whether 317 -- is it in at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is not, then it needs --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It is there. Mr. President, I have to think about this also overnight. And that is that these autopsy reports are admitted into evidence by application or submission of the Prosecution, so I think we thought of that yesterday in court [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Yes, but we are not going to change halfway now. We have now assigned D numbers. We are not going to move from D to P. Apart from that wherever the evidence comes from, the Chamber will consider it on its value, not on -- whether it is a D or a P.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No objection obviously to the assigning of a number. It is it already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could a number be assigned to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D1234.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1234 was already admitted in evidence and is now assigned this number. It is an autopsy report, Knin cemetery grave site case number KN01/317 B. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, in a wound such as this, I think you had noted previously that when you are trying to determine range, it is often difficult with no -- with just a skeleton, no flesh or saponified flesh in the wound area to determine the range because there is no burning or soot on the skin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say it is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Given the fact that that is impossible, this particular injury is one where you can't say whether or not this woman committed suicide or not.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you likewise can't say whether this was just the result of criminal activity where one person shoots another?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It could be either of these situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question in this respect, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Forgive me, Mr. Clark, that my knowledge was obtained quite a bit in the past. If someone commits suicide by putting a handgun just on his head, would that result in a certain intensity of perhaps powder remains or explosive remains even on the skull or just on the flesh or not at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be just on the skin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just on the skin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just on the skin, and it would not get any further -- certainly not in the situation of these bodies in which they had been covered by earth and in contact with other bodies. So generally the powder [indiscernible] and the burning is only seen on the skin, and would you not see it on the bone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, I just want to turn back to the statistics that you referred to. And basically, even if we refer to the statistics on page 7 and 8 of your report -- and I'm sorry, do you have that with you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, just to clarify these statistics, and referring back, if you recall, briefly to our discussion yesterday about Varivode that took place on 28th of September, 1995, because of the time elapse, even shots to the head, you couldn't tell us whether or not they took place during the Operation Storm time-frame or outside that, could you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it -- it is very difficult for you or impossible for you to say statistically what the break down of these wounds or injuries were from gunshots, the break down from -- during Operation Storm as opposed to before and after?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I haven't really attempted to do that. All I'm attempting is to analyse the bodies in the grave. There is no analysis whether this was Operation Storm or not. It's -- it -- this is the analysis of the bodies that we found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I appreciate that, Doctor, just a temporal sequence for the purposes of this case is significant. And I just wanted to add one step further to your statistics so I clarified that.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine, yes. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me just turn to these schedules, and I want to talk in some -- a little bit just about some of your schedules, the KN01, KN02 KN03. And I know that the numbers of bodies that you actually examined don't match up number for number, for instance, with the annex that is listed in page 12 and 13 for KN01. I think you looked at 186 bodies in KN01, but we have list here of 115, I believe?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now of these 115 that are here -- by the way, when the Prosecutor was putting clarification schedule together to be submitted to this Court last July, did you participate in putting that schedule together in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My first contact with this case was in October --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had no dealings with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now in this particular schedule, and I'm talking about Annex A, you have of the 115 bodies in there, 30 are unascertained.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In KN02, which is page 16, I think it's five out of six, and KN03, eight out of 14 are unascertained.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that is in addition to all of the bodies that you excluded from KN02 and KN03 even before you started to compute your numbers?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you went from 295 to 245 because you took out 30 bodies -- excuse me, 50 bodies, my math is bad. Fifty bodies from KN02 and KN03. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I compiled my report on the basis of all the findings from Knin grave site, and so the statistical analysis by and large is concerned with all of the bodies. I was asked to consider particularly KN01, and that's why these are listed, but the general comments in the report pertain to all the bodies, and I haven't done a closer analysis of the Annex A.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm interested, Doctor, in exploring just briefly some of the unascertained assessments, and if we can just look at KN02, the list being on page 13, this list being developed by you, I take it, in conjunction with the Prosecutor in November of 2008, and we noted that five out of six of these were, in fact, unascertained, and the one that the -- has a gunshot injuries to the head is 077 Milan Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gunshot injury to the legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, gunshot injury to the leg.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just as a reference point, Mr. President, can I just go into private session just very, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the interests of speed, Doctor, I just wanted to take you through several of these autopsies that are on this list that the Prosecutor has, and if we can just start with -- and I will ask you some questions after we go through them. And the first one is Milica Simic, that would be KN02/051, 65 ter 6402. Now, Doctor, this is one where another pathologist examined the -- was a fracture in the lower right limb when they note that this is unlikely that has caused the death, and the death is uncertain. In a case such as this, I mean, you cannot discount natural causes as the manner of death, could you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we offer 65 ter 6402 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That needs a number to be assigned to it. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D1235.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the autopsy report in the case KN02/051 B, which was already admitted into evidence now is assigned number -- let me just ... D1235. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. If we can move to the next one which is Mirko Supljak [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just say that that particular case, the previous one, I mean, there was a fracture of the lower leg which must have been caused in some way which perhaps takes it away from natural causes, but I certainly -- I can't exclude natural causes, but it has to be observed there is still a fracture there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right. And I understand, Doctor -- my question is you just cannot exclude natural causes from this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but if the death is unascertained, Mr. Kehoe, would it not speak for itself that it could be natural causes as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, I mean, we have all the experience not everyone breaks his leg dies from that. That is common human experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I the next question then is if this uncertain and can't exclude natural causes, and I will go through the exhibits on all these, the question remains why it is on the clarification schedule presented by the Prosecutor. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we work on the basis that if there is an unascertained death that we would not exclude for the possibility that it would be natural causes but not necessarily is by natural causes and that the probability of it might be greater or lesser depending on the type of injury found on that body. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. That is how I worded as such in my report, specifically that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That would be find, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Margetts, is what I just said, is that something -- well, whether it makes sense or not, but whether you would object against it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Mr. President. That's exactly how I understood Dr. Clark's findings to be expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I guess maybe it is an issue that we can take outside presence of the witness. It presents itself as to why the Prosecutor put these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is an argument rather than to seek the -- the experience of this witness on why the Prosecution did something, unless he is involved it in any way, and I do understand that he is not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, then I will offer into evidence 65 ter 6404, which is KN02/92 which is on the schedule, that is for Mirko Supljak. And I will offer -- the next one is Ljubica Kanezir [phoen], 65 ter 6406. 65 ter 6408 for KN.

utterances.text: One second, Mr. Kehoe. You added to the 65 ter number last time the KN number. Do you have any for 6406?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 6406 is KN02/095 B. I'm just going down the list on the Annex A for KN02.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President and my learned friend as well, of course this is the process that the Prosecution is engaging in. If it is just a matter of getting exhibit numbers for the documents already exhibited.

utterances.text: Everything on the annex is in evidence but is not yet assigned numbers.

utterances.text: As long as they are on the annex.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I can go through this list, but if we just simply go back to the individual that counsel talked about before, the Dmitar Vojnovic, the KN01/399, he is not on the witness list, but now counsel is saying he is in the scheduled killings. That's one off the top of my head. utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, it seems to be that an exceptional case. But please tell us which numbers on the annexes you would like to be assigned numbers so that they are identified as autopsy reports in evidence.

utterances.text: Yes. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's ... we're now discussing for five minutes that documents the Prosecution says are already in evidence but not yet assigned numbers and which apparently Mr. Kehoe wants to be -- wants to have in evidence, whether or not on the basis of an additional admission. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will say, Judge, that having gone through this exercise, and I don't want to take any more court time, it is a time-consuming exercise because there is really very little consistency. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do you think that just giving us now the numbers and having numbers assigned to it that we would detect these kind of exceptional circumstances? I'm afraid not. And if you say it is a time-consuming exercise that is the reason why I would not like to do it in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With Your Honours' guidance if we just say with the unascertained autopsies that are here, and I have the one, two, three, four, five -- I can read it those out and offer them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I invited you to proceed and to deal with all practical matters because there is no -- there is no dispute about it. Both parties want these autopsy reports into evidence and want to do some verifications. You're invited to do so, and then we'll receive that numbers, and then exhibit numbers will be assigned to them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will offer 65 ter 6404, 65 ter 6406, 65 ter 6408, and 65 ter 6410. Those are the autopsies for all the unascertained individuals in KN02, which is listed in page 16 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I invited you to do it out of court. You said it would take quite some time. It now -- we are waiting for that, and not for you to complete your short list. Please proceed. That's what I said before. That's what I say again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going back to the unascertained, Doctor, in KN01. And if we go back to the schedule in KN01 on page 12 and page 13, this is it the one where you said you had, I believe 30 were unascertained but were included in your assessment in KN01. And if we can go to -- again, we can go to 65 ter 6398, and I want you take a look at KN01/410 B on your list, and that is a Jovo Vujasin. And this is listed by Dr. Aiyer?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aiyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Aiyer. As uncertain. And we will offer this into evidence, and we can take it up with the Prosecutor at a later date. And if we can stay with that number, 443 and then if you just see KN01/443 B and go to 1D64- 0048. I believe we should have an English version of that. That's the English version. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could offer 1D64-0048 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like the opportunity to review the original document or log that that is derived from, and so that could be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then if we could just marked for identification, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D1236, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And let me ask you again. Was this 443, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, I'm not following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The autopsy report was referring to KN --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just verifying. Yes, yes, now I can match the names. It was 410. Let me just check on whether this is clear from the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we turn our attention to 1D64-0050.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, one second. Yes, I was a bit confused. I take it, due to page 23, line 21. If you could just verify where apparently you said KN01/443. That is what may have caused my confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That was my mistake, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That should be 410.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ten, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I had difficulties in matching the name on the list with the names we see now on our screen. But this, having been corrected, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Therefore, if we can then move to 1D64-0050. If we can blow that up a little bit. Involves the same individual, who died of cardio myopathy on 12 August, 1995. Cardio myopathy is a form of heart disease, is it not, Doctor?

utterances.text: Of course that would not show up in the autopsy?

utterances.text: With this information, Doctor, I know you had concluded that there were hospital patients, significant amount of hospital patients, in KN02 and KN03. It seems clear that they were likewise hospital patients in KN01. Does it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I mean, this form doesn't actually say she was a hospital patient. She was discharged from hospital, and she died the same day. Whether that is the same is just the wording, I don't know. I think as a general point that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I if can just ask you before you move on. The prior page that we offered into evidence 1D64-30048 had an admission date of 3 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if you look at third last line, it says released from hospital.

utterances.text: Right. And the last line it says died that day.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that doesn't necessarily mean to say that she died in hospital. It probably is that she died in hospital. If you now tell me different, that's fine. But that is it another reason why we did link them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 1D64-0050.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I would like an opportunity to review the original log so that could be marked for identification.

utterances.text: Therefore it should be MFI'd. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be exhibit number D1237, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status, for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And so just summing up what these particular various locations ending with KN01. In KN01 grave site, we had people who died from gunshot wounds, people who were uncertain, people who might have come from the hospital, people before Storm, after Storm all possibly mixed up together?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly. If you do, we didn't put a great deal of basis on the pre-burial photographs, but these are all people who, I understand, there were photographs taken, and they don't really look like people who have come out of hospital. These are bodies either in a grave or in a field somewhere with already advanced decomposition. So I think that has to be taken into context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is a fact, sir, when you're looking at the photographs, you put very little stock in the photographs to make any assessment --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is because I didn't particularly know where they came from, but it may be that they have been established or more founded than I believed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, very practical matter until now you always asked for numbers to be assigned to the autopsy reports already in evidence. utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that is 65 ter 6368. I will, in fact --

utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's for the individual we're just talking about.

utterances.text: Yes. I'm now looking -- page 23, starting on line 11, you start saying going back to -- you see that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going back to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then later on in that same paragraph, you wanted to look at KN01/410.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we have a number for that one, the autopsy report?

utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I will offer that as well. I will offer that in evidence as well. We don't -- I was somewhat --

utterances.text: I think it is in evidence because it is on the annex and the procedure we have followed until now, it is that if you present it to the witness, it will be assigned a D exhibit number and then I'll establish that it is it already in evidence but it's now accompanied by this number. utterances.text: Mr. President, it doesn't have a number, but it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.text: Yes, that is what I just said. Madam Registrar, would you assign a number to the autopsy report KN01/410 B.

utterances.text: Madam Registrar, justifiably asks for a 65 ter number. On that same line, you made reference, Mr. Kehoe, to 65 ter 6398.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 6368. And now I want to see it on my screen to know whether this is the right document, because within ten minutes, I think mistakes in numbers have been made. Yes, this is the one, and -- Madam Registrar, would you please be so kind to assign a number to 6368.

utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D1238.

utterances.text: D1238 already admitted into evidence is autopsy report, case number KN01/410 B, and has now been assigned this number. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'm not quite certain at this point if you want me to do this at the break because if I go back to those five autopsy reports that I discussed briefly I had not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Those were the ones where no questions were put to the witness and where they were considered to be more or less bar table documents, and that's the one starting with 6404 from what I remember, and we expect you to discuss them briefly with Mr. Margetts and to present them after the break so that we can assign numbers to them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, I would like to talk to you about your statistics concerning the military and non-military individuals. And I believe in your report you note -- and let me give you the exact location. Of the 245 individuals, 81 of these individuals were male soldiers, and that is on page 24 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not -- that's not the exact wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just help me out here, then. I'd like to get the exact wording down.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said almost a third of the men in the grave appeared to be soldiers as judged by the clothing they were wearing and possessions that they had. That's different from saying that they were soldiers. I'm just saying they appeared to be soldiers because of the clothing they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies on the inaccuracy. They appeared to be soldiers because of that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You weren't making a final conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, prior to this time and when you were looking at these individuals, had you been told that prior to Operation Storm there had been a full mobilization of men in the Knin area and men from 18 to 65?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I been told that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had you been told, sir, that during the course of this that in certain companies that the average age of the ARSK companies was approximately 56 years of age?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't been told that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had you been told that when you were looking at these bodies that some soldiers wore -- of the ARSK were wearing a camouflage uniform whereas others were just in a plain green uniform?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you told that the -- that the RSK police -- members of the police force that in times of war became members of the military?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, likewise, and I know that you saw some younger men, if you will, or middle-aged men, if you will, that you were in civilian clothing during in the course of the autopsies that you and your team went through.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you told during the -- before or after the examination that ARSK soldiers when they were retreating from the front lines on the 4th and 5th took their uniforms off and put civilian clothing on?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if we look at a statistic or you look at a number of all of the men that you examined with the idea that 56 could have been the average age and including people both in civilian clothes and military or police clothing, the percentage of possible soldiers that you could have examined could have gone up significantly?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly could have been higher, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me show a document which is D382 received in evidence. Now, I don't know if you've seen this document or not. This is a document -- well, we can just put it up on the screen. Take a look at it. This is a document that -- dated the 9th of January, 1996, from the Republic of Croatia Ministry of the Interior, fire-fighting and civilian protection department, list of people retrieved during hygiene and sanitary treatment of the terrain in the Zadar-Knin police administration. Now, I will tell that -- without going through the counting and you are welcome -- if we can just page through a bit, and you can just take a look at what it looks like. Go to the next page. We don't need to go through the whole thing, unless you want to. Now, in this document that is dated the 9th of January, 1996, the Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia says that 232 bodies were buried in the Knin cemetery. Now, that's significantly less, of course, than the 295 that you took out, not as far from the 245 that you said were real cases. Of the bodies you took out, there was a discrepancy between your 295 and the 232 that the Ministry of Interior said were there. Have you seen this document before? Were you shown this document?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Likewise in the Knin cemetery if we go through this D382, the listing of soldiers as opposed to your 81, they have listed 102 almost -- 44 per cent, of the bodies that were buried. Now that, sir, could -- and this is something that you don't know. That could be based on information that you didn't have concerning those particular individuals. Would that be a fair calculation as to why the discrepancy in these numbers would come?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think this is appropriate for the witness to speculate on the internal thinking or workings of this author of this document over the Croatian Ministry of Interior, so he has no information or -- there's no basis to assume he has information as to how and why the Croatian Minister of the Interior produced this document, and it's not a relevant question for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, what, apart from the arithmetic's, which everyone can do who has finished primary school. What is in the expertise or in the knowledge of this witness that would enable him to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm encouraged by your faith in my math, Judge. I wish it were so, but I'm more interested in the fact that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then rely on the Chamber's math.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm more interested in the fact that the document was not shown to the witness before he came in. But we can move on to another subject at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And thankfully, Doctor, this is the last subject. I always get a smile from Judge Orie.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have been doing most of the speaking so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, I want to chat with you about some of the things that you said yesterday which came to my attention, and if I can turn to -- if I may, I do believe I have the rough copy, and I will get the exact copy of this. But I believe you said at one point when I asked you a question, asking about gunshot wounds in war, I asked you: "These the type of injuries that you expect to see in war, aren't they?" And you answered: "Yes, partly. More obvious in war you will find many more blast injuries than bullet injuries."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that when you were going into this endeavour and looking at what you thought were remains coming from Operation Storm, you expected to find many more deaths from blast injuries than you found. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. No that was not in my mind at all. We were looking at the findings and then trying to bring some analysis afterwards. Didn't do it the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Help me out. When you are in war, you generally -- your experience has been that you find more injuries from blast --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not my experience. There are a number of well-documented papers on this, documenting major wars and battles in which it is very clear that the bulk of people, the bulk of deaths are due to blasting and explosion injury rather than to bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of course, as you say in your report on page 9 that was not your experience with the Knin cemetery?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were very few with blast injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's talk about that very briefly, and if we may, I think you say on page 24 of your report that there -- six died from blast injuries. That's in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can go back to those individual items, you list the blast injury numbers in page 9 in these -- second full paragraph, second paragraph under blast injuries, page 9. Do you see that, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the first one you have is -- well, not the first one, but one of them on there that is a possible example with less certainty, if we go to the second line is 274, KN01/274. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could bring that up on the screen. That's 65 ter 6237. And I'm interested, Doctor, in going through this of actual blast injuries of people that died in Knin. And this is one of the individuals where you note that it's less certain, but Dr. --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]

And that was largely because all other blast cases that I have seen, there has been shrapnel found in the bodies as you would expect. In this case there was none at all. And for that reason, I was less certain that it was, and I therefore, gave a sort of unascertained cause in my final listing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer 65 ter 6237 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is it already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the list, already admitted. Madam Registrar, that would receive --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D1239, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1239 is assigned to the autopsy report in case number KN01/274 B and was already admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Doctor, the Prosecutor alleges that this particular body was found in Mokro Polje which is a village well outside of Knin. Are you familiar with that area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So were you told that this particular body had -- was not -- did not perish in Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the first one on your list, KN01/385. It's 1D64-0053. This is an individual by the name of Babic, I do believe. I'm sorry ... Bibic, I apologise. Now, this is an injury, sir, that -- it notes that the cause of death --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we just scroll up on the pathologist on there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Aiyer. Sorry, Dr. Naidoo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. This is a blast injury, is it not, 1D64-0053? This is one of the ones that you included, and you also note that this individual was a soldier. I note that in your page 9 of your report where are you talking about 385. You say, All of them soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if we went on to the next page of the post-mortem report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.text: If we can offer 1D64-0053 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could a number be assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, likewise in the geography, Doctor, I mean, are you familiar with Belici which is in the Drnis municipality and that is, in fact, some distance from the town of Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go look at your -- next one, sir. This is 1D64-0082 which is KN01/392.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And I think we can also say that the other soldiers that died in Knin that we don't have additional clarification would be 396 and 426. Those other soldiers. I'm interested in some of the others that don't fall into that to try to come to some kind of number as to people who died during the shelling on Knin on the 4th and 5th, based on your examination. That's why I'm turning our attention to one in Belici, another one in Mokro Polje. And this one is in a different manner, although it's a soldier, 1D64-0082. This is an individual that died of cause of death the injuries compatible with gunshot or explosive shrapnel injuries to the head. You included as an individual that died of blast.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is somebody who looks as if he has certainly suffered blast injury but may also have been shot. Difficult to say. But there is certainly evidence of blast explosive injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, sir. If we could just page through and get an identification on this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can page -- if I might have one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The basis of him being a soldier here was the clothing, olive-green long trousers. That was the extent of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have just one moment, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to page 23 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now this -- based on identifying documentation that was included on this body, we have an identification of Rajko Trifunovic. That would have done by the anthropologists, would it not, going through their items?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who would do that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. We made no identifications in the mortuary. We recorded information, and I suspect that all these identifications were done on DNA samples by Croatian authorities, they had been given the samples by us. But we made no formal identifications at all in the mortuary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, with regard to D1239, which is KN01/274 that I stated that the body was found in Mokro Polje, I neglected to put in the actual body recovery sheet which says exactly Mokro Polje, and that is for one of the blast injuries that is set forth in Dr. Clark's report. The document is 65 ter 6239.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is not yet in evidence, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D1242.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1242, body recovery sheet, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just by way of clarity, if I can, Judge, D1242 is the recovery sheet for the autopsy that is in evidence as D1239. And my apologies for not doing that previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's on the record now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, in your report on page 9 and 24 you identify six individuals that you said died of blast injuries, five soldiers, and one civilian.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Now, of those six individuals that were -- I think -- that died of -- blast victims, I think you told us you don't know where those bodies came from?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now let us just talk a little bit about the munitions involved. Can you tell us whether or not these individuals died from, you know, tank fire or mortar fire or anti-personnel mines or booby-traps?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was one of them, I forget which number it was. It's one we've looked at who -- the main injury was to his lower leg, which might suggest a land-mine, but other than that, I can't distinguish what munitions were involved now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- that would likewise include of the five soldiers and one civilian that died, you couldn't tell us whether or not they died as a result of shrapnel from a multi-barrel rocket launcher or a Howitzer or a T-130, could you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or a grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, it may be able to be told from the nature of the shrapnel, but I can't tell that at this stage, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, thank you very much. I have no further questions. I appreciate your time.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kay --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions. Then, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic will now cross-examine you, Mr. Clark. Mr. Mikulicic is counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Clark. Given your professional expertise, can you tell what would be the typical characteristics of a cut or a epithelium wound caused by a sharp object, i.e., knife and what would be the indications of such a wound on the epithelium tissue?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a word I'm not picking up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Skin tissue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Skin tissue, sorry. A knife on the skin would -- would cut into it and leave either a stab wound or a, what we call an incised wound, a clean cut injury on the skin. In these bodies, it would be very difficult for us to see that, particularly if there were no skin or tissues, soft tissues, remaining. If the weapon had been -- gone deep enough to go into bone, then we might just see some evidence of that in the bone, but I think by and large, and these cases we would not have picked up cutting injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Based on your experience, can you tell us what would be the exact forensic procedure in order to ascertain whether a skin wound was caused by a knife or perhaps another object. Can one arrive at such a conclusion solely based on an external examination without further analysis?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are speaking in the general situation of a fresh body, if you like, we can identify perhaps the dimensions of the weapon, the knife, that caused the injury, so we could tell if it was a small weapon or a large weapon, we could tell the shape of it to some extent, but an injury caused by a sharp knife could be -- look very similar to one caused by a razor or to be caused by glass. It is not all that easy -- always easy to distinguish the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In your report, P1251, on page 9, you state in paragraph 4 that on two corpses you found certain skull injuries, suggestive of a knife or a bayonet wound. Those were the only two examples which would indicate that a sharp object, i.e., knife or bayonet were used that we can find in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is the only positive evidence of use of a knife or sharp -- sharp weapon. It has to be said that a knife going through the skull would have to be quite a thick one and a heavy weapon. But, you're correct, that is the only two that we found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask Madam Registrar to show us a 65 ter document. The number is 3385.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is an autopsy report, case number KN01/241 B. The person's name was Jovo Grubor. From the autopsy report, one concludes that gunshot wounds existed on the corpse; that is to say, there were a minimum of six, six bullet-holes on the trunk. On the comments it is also included that blunt force was exercised on the jaw. The cause of death, as stipulated, is gunshot wounds to the trunk. In this report, there is no mention of any other wounds, which would indicate that a sharp object or a knife were used. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please assign an exhibit number to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But no number assigned to it yet. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number Exhibit D1243 is an exhibit number assigned to a document already in evidence, which is an autopsy report, case number KN01/241 B. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the registrar to show us document 65 ter number 2346.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We see that this is an exhumation report. The body concerned is referred to in the autopsy report we just saw which was KN01/241 B. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please assign a number to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D1244.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Registrar for the 65 ter document, number 2143. Let us go to page 2, please, of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document contains information on the identification procedure of the corpse. It is concluded therefore that the person concerned is Jovo Grubor from the village of Plavno. At page 3 of document we can see that the corpse was identified by Dusana Grubor also from the village of Plavno. I would kindly ask for page 4 to be shown next. That is a photograph. Dr. Clark, have you had occasion to see the photograph of the corpse that we can see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes .

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When observing the photograph, in order to make your conclusions, did you also use what you could visually observe in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make much use of these photographs in doing my post-mortem report. I've since looked at these photographs and find some interesting findings in them. I don't think there is anything here which takes away from the findings in the autopsy, other than possibly irrelevant observation that this body appears to have been re-clothed after death, on the basis that there are no blood-stains at all on his shirt and with injuries to his jaw, collar-bone and hand, you would expect at least some blood-staining. But the -- what we can see in the photograph here matches with the findings at autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Dr. Clark, the wound we can see on the right-hand side of the shirt right under the chin, does it indicate to you, as an expert that it might be a wound that was caused by a knife or another sharp object?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to see the detail here. I think it's more likely a gunshot injury, which is initially struck the chin and has then struck the collar-bone. I think that was the interpretation of the pathologist that this was a wound going through the chin, down into the collar-bone into the chest, and you can just see a wound under the V of -- of his shirt, and it is possible that his hand was in the way and was injured at the same time. But there is nothing particularly to suggest that that is a sharp -- sharp weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Dr. Clark, you have carried out a number of autopsies. Did you come across any injuries in at least one single case which would indicate that a person was killed after being wounded by several bullets in the trunk, in the upper part of the body, and that, in addition, that person sustained neck injuries indicative of the use of a knife, that the throat was slit. Did you come across such an example while undertaking the exercise of autopsies in the area of Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none at all. Having said that, we probably would not have seen in the remains any evidence of a cut-throat injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please assign a number for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D1245.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1245 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you for your answers, Dr. Clark. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, may I just interrupt one moment before my learned friend comes in, and I apologise again. Before the break we were talking about the autopsy for KN01/392 which was 1D64-0082. It is one that Dr. Clark did, in fact, comment on, and I neglected to put that in evidence prior to the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat the number. You pronounced it that quickly that I'm not quite sure that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 1D64-0082 which is the autopsy report for KN01/392.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I heard you said 392, but you did it that quickly that I hardly can think of even think of blaming madam transcriber for not catching up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It is not in evidence, and we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Not in evidence. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1246.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1246 is admitted into evidence. Yes. Before, however, I give an opportunity to you, Mr. Margetts, to -- to re-examine the witness, I have one question for him. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No inaccuracies, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No inaccuracies. Thank you very much. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I only have one matter that I'd like to raise with Dr. Clark that arises from the issue regarding Dmitar Vojnovic which is killing number 248, the number ascribed by the Croatian authorities, and we dealt with this -- Mr. Kehoe dealt with this killing and referenced the autopsy report KN01/216, I believe. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, it is KN01/162 for this individual. Which is D12 -- excuse me. KN01/162 which is D1226, and 1227, I believe, is the identifying document. It is the record-keeping in this endeavour concerning autopsies has been difficult to say the least and before any type of -- frankly I don't have that document here because it wasn't on the list, but in any event, I need to be able to go back and take a look through those. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- let's invite Mr. Margetts to proceed, and let's see where it brings us and where mention -- reference was made to KN01/216. Now, Mr. Kehoe, you say that is KN01/162.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: KN03 -- excuse me, 162 is what I introduced into evidence under D1226 with the identifying information 1227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would suggest the following: Every document to be discussed from now on on this matter, I'd like to see it on the screen so that we know what we're talking about. utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, if I could please have 65 ter 6787 presented on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Dr. Clark, can you see the autopsy report that is presented on the screen? It's --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: A body exhumed from the location KN01 and assigned the number 399. Could you review that and could you confirm that that is an autopsy report that was prepared by a member of your team?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And in regard to the conclusions, do you differ with those conclusions or do you concur with those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CLARK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I agree entirely with the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Clark.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we've had discussions with the Defence in relation to this set of documents, so I'd move this document into evidence and seek an exhibit number. I'd understand if my learned friend wanted it to be marked for identification at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have no problem at this point just marking it marked for identification. I would just like to go back and cross-reference it. Because, again, I am not certain that we are talking about the same Dmitar Vujanovic, and I'd like to go back and see what I can find out looking through the rest of this document because I simply don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Colonel Konings, I'd like to begin in focussing on the nature of artillery weapons. If you could please refer to your expert report, and if we could please have P1259, MFI.
